data.title: A small company that likes feeding people.
data.intro: Food Culture Tours is six hosts in five towns. We take small groups into the markets, kitchens and tables where we eat ourselves.

children.text: We started with one market walk on Tuesdays in Marenta. People asked if they could come back and cook, so we added a kitchen. Then they asked about lunch, then about other towns. Each new place came from a host we already knew.
How we work
Groups are never larger than twelve, and most are eight or fewer. That is how many people can stand at a market stall without blocking it, and how many can sit at one table and hear each other.
We buy from the same producers every week and we pay them the price on the stall. When we bring a group, they know us by name and they have time to talk.
Hosts are named on every experience page. If you want one host in particular, say so when you ask for a date.
Food and hosts

Every experience has a vegetarian version. Vegan and gluten-free versions are marked yes or ask on each experience page. We cook with wheat, eggs, dairy, nuts and shellfish in most kitchens and cannot promise an allergen-free table.

Tell us early
Write to us about allergies and diets when you ask for a date, not on the morning. We read every enquiry and reply with what we can and cannot do on that experience.
What we cannot promise

Our kitchens handle wheat, eggs, dairy, tree nuts, sesame, fish and shellfish. Traces can be present in any dish. If a reaction could be serious, we will say plainly that a tour may not be safe for you.
Children
Children of any age may join the market walks and long lunches with an adult. Cooking classes are for ages ten and up with an adult.

data.title: Morning at the Piazza Market
data.summary: Walk the weekday market with Giulia, meet three producers and finish with a tasting at a shared table.
data.tastes:
Sheep's cheese with warm bread
Blood oranges and early lemons
Olives from the Ferrante family stall
Coffee and a small almond cake
data.meeting_point: Fountain of the Four Lemons, Piazza Verde
data.meeting_note: Giulia wears a green apron and carries a woven market basket.
data.intro: The market in Piazza Verde runs from seven until one. We arrive when the stalls are still being set up, because that is when the producers have time to talk. You taste as you go and can buy what you like to take home.

children.text: What the morning looks like
We start at the fountain and walk the market in a loop, stopping at three stalls that Giulia has bought from for years. At each one the producer explains what is in season and what to ask for.
The tasting at the end happens at a long table in the old grain store behind the square. Bread, cheese, fruit and coffee. Nothing is rushed, and the group is never more than eight.

data.title: Fresh Pasta by Hand
data.summary: Learn to roll, fill and shape two kinds of pasta with Luca, then eat what you made at his long table.
data.tastes:
Egg pasta, rolled and cut by hand
Filled pasta with ricotta and herbs
A plain tomato sauce
A glass of local white wine, or juice
data.meeting_point: Luca's kitchen, 4 Via del Forno, San Tiberio
data.meeting_note: The green door next to the bakery. Ring the bell twice.
data.intro: Luca teaches the way his grandmother taught him: no scales, a lot of flour on the table and a lot of patience. Everyone makes their own dough and shapes their own pasta.

children.text: Before you book

The dough uses wheat flour and eggs. If you need a gluten-free or egg-free version, tell us when you enquire and Luca will say honestly what he can change. We will not promise a table free of flour dust.
Aprons are provided. Wear shoes you can stand in for a few hours.

data.title: Long Lunch on the Terrace
data.summary: Four courses of market vegetables and the morning's fish, served at one table above the sea.
data.tastes:
Marinated anchovies or artichokes
A pasta course
Grilled fish, or a vegetable main
Lemon cake and coffee
data.meeting_note: Ask for the table with the blue cloth. Your host is Giulia or Anna.
data.intro: One long table, one menu that changes with the market, and nobody checking the time. Most guests stay until after three.

children.text: How the lunch works
The menu is set each morning after Giulia visits the market and the harbour. We tell you the dishes when you arrive, and you tell us what you cannot eat.
Wine is poured with each course. A non-alcoholic pairing is always available.

data.title: Tomato and Basil Kitchen
data.summary: Cook a tomato lunch with Tomas: a cold soup, tomato bread, a slow stew and a salad from the garden.
data.tastes:
Cold tomato soup with olive oil
Bread rubbed with ripe tomato
Slow tomato and bean stew
Garden salad with basil
data.meeting_point: Casa Almina, 17 Calle del Huerto, Torre Almina
data.meeting_note: A blue gate beside the water tower. Tomas will be at the gate at ten to eleven.
data.intro: Tomas grows the tomatoes himself, so the class starts in the garden with a basket. Most of the menu is vegetarian by default, and every dish can be made vegan and gluten-free.

data.title: Spice and Garlic Stalls
data.summary: A short morning at the harbour stalls with Nikos: dried herbs, garlic, chili and the cheese that goes with them.
data.tastes:
Mountain tea and dried oregano
Garlic, chili and capers
Goat's cheese and thick yogurt
Honey on warm bread
data.meeting_point: The blue ferry kiosk on the quay, Thalia Bay
data.meeting_note: Nikos has a grey beard and a canvas shopping bag.
data.intro: A small harbour market where most of the stalls are run by the people who picked or made what they sell. Nikos takes you to the ones he buys from.

data.title: Cheese Counter Walk
data.summary: Visit a cheese counter, a bakery and a cured-meat shop with Luca, and learn how to order at each one.
data.tastes:
Three cheeses, young to aged
Two kinds of bread
Cured meats (a vegetarian plate is available)
A small glass of local wine or juice
data.meeting_point: Piazza del Pozzo, by the well, San Tiberio
data.meeting_note: Luca carries a clipboard with the route on it. The route is not secret.
data.intro: This one is for people who want to feel at ease in a food shop. We stop at three counters and Luca teaches the words you need: how much, how ripe, how it is usually eaten.

data.title: Three Days on the Marenta Coast
data.summary: Three days and two nights in a family hotel: the market, a cooking class and the terrace lunch, with free time between.
data.runs: Every other Friday, April to October
data.tastes:
Day one: market morning and a harbour walk
Day two: pasta class and the terrace lunch
Day three: lemon terraces and a farewell breakfast
data.meeting_note: Anna meets the group in the lobby at six in the evening on the day before.
data.intro: A relaxed long weekend. The food days are in the morning and at midday, and the afternoons are yours for swimming, walking or sleeping. Two nights in a small hotel, breakfast and four meals included.

children.text: What is included
Two nights in a shared-bathroom family hotel or a private room for a supplement, breakfast every day, the market morning, the pasta class and the terrace lunch, and the lemon terrace walk.
Flights, transfers to Marenta and drinks outside the meals are not included.

data.title: Five Days in the Hill Towns
data.summary: Five days and four nights between three hill towns, with a cooking class, an olive mill visit and one long lunch each day.
data.tastes:
Pasta, bread and a slow Sunday sauce
Olive oil from the press
Cheese from the hill farms
A different long table every day
data.meeting_note: Luca meets the group at the well at five in the afternoon.
data.intro: We move by minibus between San Tiberio and two smaller towns, with one meal and one activity each day. The groups are small so we can eat at family tables, not restaurants.

data.title: Lunch with a Stallholder
data.summary: Shop the harbour market with Ines, then eat a long lunch at the home of a stallholder who has sold there for forty years.
data.tastes:
Grilled sardines or grilled vegetables
Rice cooked with the day's shellfish, or with beans
Bread, olives and salted almonds
Egg and cinnamon pudding
data.meeting_note: Ines wears a red scarf and holds a paper bag from the bakery.
data.intro: Six places at a family table. You shop first, so you know where the lunch came from, and you eat in a home, not a dining room.

data.title: Sunday Table: Cook and Eat
data.summary: A relaxed class where the group cooks one big shared meal and sits down to it at two o'clock.
data.tastes:
A rice dish cooked in a wide pan
Roasted vegetables with almond sauce
Fried dough with honey
Wine, juice and coffee
data.meeting_point: Casa Almina, 17 Calle del Huerto, Torre Almina
data.meeting_note: A blue gate beside the water tower. Tomas will be at the gate at half past ten.
data.intro: A slower class for groups of friends and families. Children from ten years old can join if an adult comes with them.

data.title: Marenta Coast
data.blurb: A steep coastal town of lemon terraces, with a produce market every morning and a harbour where the boats land before dawn.

data.title: San Tiberio
data.blurb: A hill town of stone lanes, bakeries and olive mills, about an hour inland from the coast.

data.title: Vila Raposa
data.blurb: A fishing and farming town at the mouth of a river. The harbour market opens at six in the morning.

data.title: Torre Almina
data.blurb: A walled town of tomato farms and orange groves, where lunch starts late and ends later.

data.title: Thalia Bay
data.blurb: A small island harbour with herb sellers, goat's cheese and fishing boats unloading at the quay.

data.title: Giulia
data.bio: Giulia grew up above a fruit stall in Piazza Verde. She knows which grower has the first figs and which one only sells to regulars.

data.title: Luca
data.bio: Luca ran a bakery kitchen for twelve years before he started teaching. He cooks for a table of eight the same way he cooks for his family.

data.title: Ines
data.bio: Ines worked the harbour market as a teenager and still knows every stallholder by name. She plans each lunch around what came off the boats that morning.

data.title: Tomas
data.bio: Tomas farms tomatoes and beans outside Torre Almina and teaches in his own garden kitchen. He talks about soil more than most people talk about recipes.

data.title: Nikos
data.bio: Nikos has run the quay stalls' unofficial tour for years, usually for friends who visit. He started doing it properly when the friends began to bring friends.

data.title: Anna
data.bio: Anna answers the enquiries, builds multi-day trips and meets groups at the hotel. She is the person to write to about diets, access and dates.
